current.title: How Much Of 'You' Is Actually New
current.hook: 330 billion of your cells vanish every single day.
current.closing: So technically, your skin is younger than your phone.
current.question: How old are your oldest cells? Guess below.

held_for: judge: This is a chart deck about cell renewal: overlapping unreadable labels, a mascot who is never the cause of anything, and a closing about skin being younger than your phone that the visuals never set up.

judge.one_line: This is a chart deck about cell renewal: overlapping unreadable labels, a mascot who is never the cause of anything, and a closing about skin being younger than your phone that the visuals never set up.
problems: The hook frames leave the bottom half of the screen empty under a stock ribcage. No motion or reason to stay beyond icons fading in, and the mascot is absent.
seg1:start labels overprint each other ('120 d28 d5 days', 'Red blood cellSkStomach lining'), so they cannot be read.
seg1:mid: the '5 day' and '28 days' labels collide and the mascot stands on them. The scene is a bubble chart with one giant disc.
seg2 is a plain two-bar chart, and the mascot floats beside it with no bit.
seg3 is titled 'New cells per day' but plots a cumulative total. The mascot merely rides the line's tip.
seg4 bubbles repeat seg3's numbers and get cut off by the caption band. The 'skin younger than your phone' line has no visual (no phone, no skin).
fixes: Open on motion: a body in which a visible wave of cells blinks out and is replaced, with a counter racing toward 330 billion and Data sweeping the old cells away with a broom.
Rebuild seg1 as one body with four tissue zones that refresh at their own rates as Data cranks a day-counter. Give every label a measured, non-overlapping slot.
seg2: an old, unchanged neuron next to a skin patch that Data peels and replaces dozens of times over the same span.
seg3: Data shovels new cells into a body-shaped vessel that fills to 30T by Day 100. Retitle it as a cumulative total.
seg4: put a phone next to a skin patch with age badges (skin 28 days versus the phone's age) to land the punchline. Keep every mark inside the safe area above the caption band.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.

PACE: each SAY is ONE spoken sentence of at most 16 words — the number and what it means, nothing else; the HOOK at most 14 words, the CLOSING at most 10, the QUESTION at most 8. A beat is on screen about 8 seconds; a longer line is refused. Each SAY says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'.
